penetration_assumption: A new exotic vegetable line at ARY sells like the MEDIAN exotic ARY already stocks — about Rs 1,400/yr, i.e. ~28 buyers a year at ~Rs 50 a purchase out of 4,700 residents (0.6% annual penetration). VERIFIED analogue set (live 12m, group 159): Parwal Rs 11,984 / Broccoli Rs 11,170 / Drum Sticks Rs 3,499 / Ivy Gourd Rs 1,638 / Capsicum Red & Yellow Rs 1,573 / Green Pods Rs 1,275 / Contola Rs 1,104 / Snake Gourd Rs 554 / Singre Rs 512 / Lettuce Rs 413 — median Rs 1,406, mean Rs 3,372. Broccoli is the CEILING, not the average: it is the most mainstream exotic (canteen staple). Zucchini, celery, leek, kohlrabi are all narrower than broccoli on a rural Punjabi Sikh campus. Build-up: 9 narrow lines x Rs 1,400 = Rs 12,600, plus 2 semi-mainstream (baby corn, cherry tomato) x Rs 8,000 = Rs 16,000, plus re-stocking the dormant Pudina (fresh mint) at ~25% of coriander's Rs 35,558 x its 47% availability = Rs 7,000. Total ~Rs 36,000/yr = 0.05% of a Rs 7.67 Cr business. Margin at 15% (generous: Broccoli, the true analogue, is VERIFIED at 12.5%) = Rs 5,400 gross profit. This is ESTIMATED. It is also almost certainly net-NEGATIVE: exotics with 3-5 day shelf life at 0.6% penetration would shrink 30-50%, i.e. ~Rs 8,600 of loss on ~Rs 24,650 of purchases against Rs 5,400 of gross profit. The decision is robust across the whole plausible range — even at 5x my estimate the gross profit is ~Rs 27,000/yr.
probe_evidence:
FIRST, A TOOL BUG THAT INVALIDATES THE INPUT DIFF: `ary assort probe` AND-s multiple terms despite its help text stating "Several terms are OR-ed". `probe oyster shiitake button mushroom` -> 0 SKUs; `probe mushroom` -> 21 SKUs, Rs 98,836, last sale 2026-08-30. Every multi-word probe I ran first returned a false zero, including `lemon nimbu galgal lime` (0) vs `lemon` (146 SKUs). Anyone probing multi-word will manufacture exactly the false-missing verdicts this exercise exists to prevent. All probes below were re-run ONE TERM AT A TIME and confirmed by direct SQL over the full 21,479-SKU master.

THE INPUT COVERAGE DIFF IS UNUSABLE — its evidence strings are visibly bogus name-matches: "Garlic" matched on the word 'rajasthan'; "Radish" on 'white' (Rs 34.8 L); "Cauliflower" and "Cabbage" and "Lettuce" all on 'head'; "Green chilli" on 'desi'; "Brinjal" on 'purple'; "Bathua" on 'winter'; "Yam" on 'cut'; "Okra" on 'ladies'; "S/E Indian vegetables" on 'east'. I discarded it and rebuilt from the catalogue.

WHAT THE CATALOGUE ACTUALLY SHOWS (VERIFIED): group 159 "Vegetable" holds 1,333 SKUs but only 91 ACTIVE. The 1,242 inactive are NOT a dormant assortment — they are legacy per-price-point records from an old system ("Vegetables Palak 2272", "Vegetables Palak 2277" ... 96 of them for palak alone, 87 for cauliflower, 75 for ladyfinger). One commodity, exploded into historical rows. Reading them as 1,242 addable lines would be the single biggest error available here.

COVERAGE IS NEAR-TOTAL. 70 of 91 active vegetable SKUs sold in the live window. Every commodity in the demand research has a live, selling SKU. Differently-named matches the diff missed: shalgam=Turnip, arvi=Arbi, bathua=Bathu Saag, chaulai=Cholai Saag, tindora=Ivy Gourd (Kundru), sahjan=Drum Sticks, ganth=absent but kachalu/arbi present, spring onion=Leafy Onion (Rs 5,826), beetroot=Chukander (Rs 35,097), ash gourd=Chappan Kaddu/Petha. Fresh LEMON exists as ProductID 0643 filed under **Fruit**, not Vegetable — Trap 1 exactly. Frozen peas/mixed veg/sweet corn are covered by Pagro + Mannsfield + McCain in group 128, so a freezer demonstrably exists.

GENUINELY ABSENT — 11 lines, direct SQL over all 21,479 SKUs, all returning 0: zucchini/courgette 0, celery/ajmod 0, leek 0, kohlrabi/knol/ganth 0, baby corn 0, curry leaf/kadi patta/meetha neem 0, cherry tomato 0, oyster/shiitake/button mushroom 0, iceberg/romaine 0, fresh dill/suva 0, chopped-veg pack 0. (sprout=1 SKU Rs 180; "organic"=50 SKUs but none are vegetables.) Every one of these is tagged nice-to-have in the research and aimed at the "university | staff" cohort.

LISTED BUT DORMANT — 21 active SKUs with zero 12m sales. Only ONE is a real fresh-produce miss: **Pudina (fresh mint)**, active and never stocked. **Potato Pahdi** (hill potato) is also dormant but plain Potato already sells Rs 1.55 L, so it is cannibalisation not incremental. The rest are legacy duplicates (Tomato 2267, Tori 2268/2269, Cabbage 2239, Mehti, Suger Beet, Capsicum Small) or frozen-snack items with live equivalents in group 128.

THE AVAILABILITY EVIDENCE THAT DECIDES THE VERDICT (store open 354 of 365 days, VERIFIED): Hara Dhania (coriander) — the highest-frequency vegetable purchase in any Indian store, tagged must-have/daily — sold on only **166 days = 46.9%**. Palak 126 days (35.6%). Mushroom 178 (50.3%). Radish 179 (50.6%). Matar 192. Pumpkin 197. Lady Finger 206. Arbi/Brinjal 212. Bitter Gourd 217. Cucumber 244. Cauliflower 246. Carrot 253. Capsicum 265. Ginger and Green Chilli 270. Garlic 278. Only Onion (349), Potato (345) and Tomato (335) clear 90%. Stock on hand right now is 754 units across 106 SKUs — roughly ONE DAY of cover. Bringing the 19 year-round lines to 90% availability is worth Rs 3,27,090/yr gross arithmetic (ESTIMATED; realistically Rs 1.5-2 L after a substitution haircut) — 5-9x the entire assortment gap, with zero new SKUs, zero new suppliers and zero new licence.
top_skus: Curry leaves / kadi patta — genuinely absent, 0 matches in 21,479 SKUs; the only absent line I would actually defend adding (cooking staple for South Indian teaching staff, ~Rs 10/bunch, trivial trial cost)
Pudina / fresh mint — LISTED AND ACTIVE, zero sales in 12 months; restock, do not re-add. The only real fresh-produce dormancy in the category
Baby corn — absent, semi-mainstream, ~Rs 8,000/yr at broccoli-like penetration
Cherry tomato — absent, ~Rs 8,000/yr, but needs 4-8C chiller
Zucchini — absent; the input diff's ONLY 'missing' verdict, and it is correct, but it is a nice-to-have worth ~Rs 1,400/yr
Iceberg / romaine lettuce — absent; ARY's one generic 'Lettuce' SKU did Rs 413 on 6 days, which is the honest forecast
Celery, leek, kohlrabi, oyster/shiitake mushroom, fresh dill — absent, all ~Rs 500-1,400/yr each, all below the cost of carrying them

Cut / washed / chopped vegetable packs — absent; the research calls this the best value-added idea, but the whole saag complex (Sarso Rs 4,619 + Palak Rs 12,451 + Methi Rs 9,290 + Bathu Rs 296) is only Rs 26,656/yr, so a premium pack on ~30% of it is ~Rs 8,000
blockers: ECONOMICS, NOT LICENCE — the category barely breaks even. VERIFIED from the live purchase ledger (PurchaseDetail.ItemValue vs SaleDetail.FinalSaleAmount, 2025-09-01 to 2026-08-31): sales Rs 27,22,050, COGS on what sold Rs 24,27,241, gross profit Rs 2,94,809 = **10.83% blended GM**. Purchases Rs 28,21,140, so Rs 3,93,899 of vegetables were bought and never sold = **13.96% shrink**. Gross profit Rs 2.95 L against Rs 3.94 L of unsold stock: vegetables at ARY are at best marginally profitable today. Adding slow exotic SKUs to that is value-destructive.

THE RESEARCH OVER-ASSUMED MARGIN BY ~2x — it bands greens at 25-40% and ginger/garlic at 18-30%. VERIFIED per-SKU reality: Onion 13.0%, Tomato 15.7%, Potato 15.9%, Ginger 15.2%, Garlic 15.0%, Green Chilli 13.7%, Hara Dhania 2.7%, Broccoli 12.5%, Drum Sticks 7.4%. Retail lines cluster 12-17%; the best in the category is Leafy Onion at 22.2%. Any revenue-times-30% sizing built on the demand file is roughly double reality.

CHILLER IS THE PHYSICAL PREREQUISITE AND IS UNPROVEN — a FREEZER is confirmed (McCain, Pagro frozen peas/mixed veg/sweet corn, Mannsfield 5kg, all active in group 128). A 4-8C CHILLER is NOT-CHECKED and cannot be established from this database. Six of the eleven absent lines (cherry tomato, iceberg lettuce, celery, fresh dill, sprouts, exotic mushrooms) will not hold 48 hours without one.

SUPPLIER REACH FROM RAJGARH — zucchini, celery, leek, cherry tomato and oyster/shiitake mushroom come from polyhouse growers or the Delhi/Chandigarh wholesale trade, not the Rajgarh/Solan mandi that supplies ARY today. That is a new supply line, on a hill road, for ~Rs 29,000 of annual revenue.

NO SHELF BUFFER — Stock.Quantity (the real on-hand; ProductMaster.QuantityOnHand is dead) totals 754 units across 106 vegetable SKUs. That is about one day of cover. A store that cannot keep coriander on the shelf 53% of days has a replenishment problem, and adding 11 slow lines to that shelf makes it worse, not better.

DEMAND STRUCTURE CAPS THE UPSIDE — Rs 9,11,709 of the Rs 27.2 L of 'vegetable sales' is just 12 bills: monthly institutional bulk (the _Z SKUs) to the campus mess, at 0.5-8.9% margin, essentially a pass-through. True RETAIL vegetable sales are Rs 18,10,341 across 32,740 bills = **Rs 32 per resident per month**. The langar/mess feeds most of the campus, so the population that cooks at home — and would ever buy zucchini — is a structural minority. This is why per-line exotic penetration is 0.6%, not the 5-10% the research implicitly assumes.

CAPITAL IS NOT A BLOCKER, AND SAYING SO MATTERS — opening stock for all 11 lines is roughly Rs 25,000. Nothing here is gated on money; it is gated on whether the lines earn their shelf, and they do not.
kill_reason: Not a kill, but the assortment thesis for vegetables is dead: the category is COVERED and the real defect is AVAILABILITY. Three independent proofs. (1) COVERAGE — 70 of 91 active SKUs sold in the live 12-month window and every commodity in the demand research has a live selling SKU; the diff's "missing" verdicts were bad name-matches ("Garlic" matched on 'rajasthan', "Radish" on 'white', "Cauliflower" on 'head'), and the differently-named ones resolve cleanly (shalgam=Turnip, arvi=Arbi, bathua=Bathu Saag, chaulai=Cholai Saag, tindora=Ivy Gourd, beetroot=Chukander, spring onion=Leafy Onion, and fresh lemon sitting in the **Fruit** subgroup — Trap 1). Only 11 lines are genuinely absent by direct SQL over all 21,479 SKUs, and all 11 are nice-to-have exotics worth ~Rs 36,000/yr combined = 0.05% of a Rs 7.67 Cr business. (2) THE 1,242 "DORMANT" SKUs ARE AN ILLUSION — they are legacy per-price-point records ("Vegetables Palak 2272" x96, cauliflower x87, ladyfinger x75), one commodity per subgroup exploded into history, not addable lines. Exactly one active fresh SKU is a real dormancy: Pudina. (3) AVAILABILITY IS THE DEFECT — with the store open 354 days, coriander (must-have, daily, the classic "if they don't have dhania they don't have vegetables" trust signal) was on the shelf **166 days = 46.9%**; palak 35.6%, mushroom 50.3%, cucumber 68.9%, cauliflower 69.5%, ginger and green chilli 76.3%, garlic 78.5%. Only onion, potato and tomato clear 90%. On-hand stock is 754 units = ~1 day of cover. Closing that availability gap on the 19 year-round lines is worth Rs 3,27,090/yr gross arithmetic (Rs 1.5-2 L after an honest substitution haircut) versus Rs 36,000 for the entire assortment build — 5-9x the return, with no new SKU, no new supplier, no chiller and no licence. And the category's own P&L says stop adding: 10.83% blended GM producing Rs 2,94,809 of gross profit against Rs 3,93,899 of vegetables bought and never sold (13.96% shrink). The recommendation is to fix replenishment on coriander, palak, mushroom and cucumber, restock the already-listed Pudina, trial curry leaves, and add nothing else. NOTE FOR THE NEXT LANE: `ary assort probe` AND-s its terms despite documenting them as OR-ed — every multi-word probe returns a false zero. Probe one word at a time until that is fixed.
